statement: Removing a canceled head triggers a rescan only when size exceeds cur, so at full weight there is no rescan.
A zero head fits when free weight equals zero.
For a live Acquire whose fast path failed and weight exceeds size, the call waits only on context cancellation outside the queue.
A negative weight admitted through the fast path decreases the aggregate charged weight.
Release writes the subtracted value before testing for negative charged weight.
Release unlocks before panicking on negative charged weight, with no restoration.
Feasible overlapping Acquire calls allocate separate queue entries without a caller identifier.
The context callback Done runs before the semaphore mutex is acquired.
Queued cancellation calls Context.Err after releasing the mutex.
When cancellation wins the queued select after a ready grant, the weight is subtracted again from the held total and notification runs.
After receiving ready, Acquire checks Done and calls Release if it is closed before returning Err.
TryAcquire checks capacity and queue length under a potentially blocking mutex.
The notifier leaves remaining waiters blocked when the first queued request cannot fit.
A successful fast-path acquisition need not recheck Done after charging weight.
A Release of zero can invoke notification while leaving the aggregate charge unchanged.
Release has no caller identity argument and subtracts from the aggregate charge regardless of holder identity.
A notified waiter is removed from the queue before its Ready channel is closed.
Acquire samples the supplied Context's Done channel and has no request-identity check.
